idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), error rate 18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error after us-east, which left the regions on mixed versions. A retry finished the rollout. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and look into the orchestrator error that stopped the rollback.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and is healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open.

- **Version choice:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. The bad version, v2.3.1, was the latest deploy. Its release candidate had also failed in staging.
- **Rollback:** The first attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, which left the regions on different versions. Rolling back to the same version is safe to repeat, so I retried, and the second attempt finished. us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. The service now passes health checks, and the error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. The first request timed out, so I resent it with the same idempotency key, which prevents a duplicate. The incident list confirms only one was created. Its description covers the failure, the rollback (including the partial failure and retry) and two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and look into the orchestrator error.

content.text: The rollback stopped partway. us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version again is safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
